mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate compresses the discount rate applied to equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship is consistent across all monetary policy regimes and does not require a specific threshold.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day forward returns is negative or below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% within the past month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a sell-off in equities due to reduced consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth is weak (INDPRO below 100) and retail sales growth is weak (RSAFS below 540000 million dollars), the market anticipates a recession, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is driven by the joint weakness in supply and demand.
failure_condition: The interaction term (INDPRO * RSAFS) fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined as FEDFUNDS rising above 2.5% and increasing for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate profitability and higher borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS increased in the last month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances during the tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1.5 million units signals weak residential construction, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST below 1500 fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (INDPRO below 95), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic output and inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 95.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 265, it signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 265.

mechanism_narrative: A weak payroll employment growth (less than 100 thousand new jobs in the past month) signals a deteriorating labor market, causing immediate negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth < 100.
